perspective:
Cynthia Huber’s available information:

- She is a teacher at the community center, teaching evening classes. She knows Christina Gonzalez as the center’s marketing manager and a colleague. They are not personally close and have had professional disagreements about programs and community engagement.
- Cynthia values traditional teaching methods, structure, and depth. She initially believes traditional classes should be prominently featured in the upcoming semester’s marketing materials.
- In the staff meeting, she hears Christina argue for showcasing dynamic, interactive sessions and finding a balance. Cynthia responds by defending traditional classes as proven, appealing to long-time attendees, and aligned with the core audience’s values. She is not convinced by Christina’s approach.
- Cynthia later observes positive feedback from Christina’s innovative marketing campaign. She approaches Christina to learn what was done differently.
- She hears Christina say the campaign focused on interactive elements, social media engagement, and creating conversation rather than just broadcasting information. Cynthia acknowledges Christina captured both depth and appeal.
- Christina tells Cynthia that blending new and old methods means they can learn from each other.
- Cynthia proposes a joint pilot project combining traditional lectures with interactive online sessions. She hears Christina support the idea as a way to test blending their methods. Cynthia hopes it will enhance learning and attract a wider audience.
- Cynthia knows the pilot project succeeded. She tells Christina they should scale it immediately and says she will organize resources and set up a schedule. She hears Christina say she will coordinate with the marketing team.
- Cynthia knows feedback after implementation has been overwhelmingly positive. She prepares a presentation to showcase the project’s success and advocate expansion to other centers. She discusses this with Christina and hears Christina offer help and agree other centers could benefit.
- Cynthia feels proud and sees the project as proof that blending traditional and innovative methods was the right move.

Excluded from Cynthia’s perspective: Christina’s private thoughts, motives, MBTI, education, or any information Christina did not say or Cynthia did not observe.
